related_questions.question: What is the #1 cause of depression?
related_questions.snippet: There's no single cause of depression. It can occur for a variety of reasons and it has many different triggers. For some people, an upsetting or stressful life event, such as bereavement, divorce, illness, redundancy and job or money worries, can be the cause. Different causes can often combine to trigger depression.

related_questions.question: What is the COVID anxiety syndrome?

text_blocks.snippet: COVID Anxiety Syndrome (CAS) is characterized by maladaptive coping strategies, such as avoidance and perseveration, in response to the perceived threat of COVID-19. It's a specific form of anxiety related to the pandemic, distinct from general anxiety about COVID-19. CAS can involve behaviors like excessive handwashing, social isolation, and constant checking for symptoms, even when not necessary.
snippet_highlighted_words: characterized by maladaptive coping strategies, such as avoidance and perseveration, in response to the perceived threat of COVID-19

list.title: Maladaptive Coping:
list.snippet: CAS involves unhelpful or excessive ways of dealing with the perceived threat of COVID-19.

list.title: Perseveration:
list.snippet: This refers to repetitive, often intrusive thoughts or actions related to the virus, like repeatedly checking for symptoms.

list.title: Avoidance:
list.snippet: Individuals with CAS may avoid situations or places they perceive as risky, even if those places are not actually dangerous.

list.title: Distinction from General Anxiety:
list.snippet: CAS is a specific type of anxiety related to the pandemic, rather than just general anxiety that may be present.

list.title: Potential for Persistence:
list.snippet: Even as the pandemic wanes, CAS can linger and affect individuals' lives.

text_blocks.snippet: While long COVID can also include anxiety and depression, CAS is distinct from the mental health impacts of the virus itself.
